- VCO1 LEVEL 9, VCO2 LEVEL 9: both VCOs (voltage-controlled oscillators) near full, which pushes more into the filters than they take cleanly. This is level and drive at once; backing them off cleans the riff up.
- TIME 0: no portamento, so notes step cleanly.
- Listen for: a fat, slightly gritty buzz.

steps.title: Nasal high-pass, screaming low-pass
steps.why:
The high-pass adds a nasal honk and the low-pass is set to scream.
- CUTOFF (HPF) 3.5 · 135 Hz, PEAK 4: the high-pass filter (HPF) removes everything below its cutoff, clearing the rumble. PEAK is Korg’s word for resonance; here it gives a honk just above the cutoff. Raise the cutoff towards 5 for a thin, nasal riff.
- CUTOFF (LPF) 5 · 600 Hz: the low-pass filter (LPF) removes everything above; the resting brightness between flicks.
- PEAK (LPF) 7: the scream. Above about 8.5 it whistles over the notes.
- FILTER 2: the harder circuit, which distorts sooner.
- Listen for: play a note and switch between FILTER 1 and FILTER 2 to hear how much harder the second circuit bites.

steps.title: A flick on every note
steps.why:
Envelope 2 (EG2, the main envelope) flicks the low-pass open on every note and falls back quickly. Each note starts with a sharp “yow” and holds a gritty tone behind it.
- EG2/EXT (LPF mod) 5: the size of the “yow”.
- ATTACK (EG2) 0 · 5 ms: instant.
- HOLD 0, DECAY 4.1 · 150 ms, SUSTAIN 5: back to half within about 150 ms. DECAY is how long the “yow” lasts.
- RELEASE (EG2) 1.8 · 120 ms: short, to keep sixteenth notes apart.
- Listen for: play a fast riff; each note barks and then snarls.

steps.title: Send the output into the preamp
steps.why:
The output is sent into the external signal processor (ESP), whose preamp saturates whatever it is given.
- Cable SIGNAL OUT → SIGNAL IN: the synth’s own output goes round into the processor.
- SIGNAL LEVEL 5: how hard the preamp is driven, and so how torn the held tone gets once the loop is closed.
- Listen for: on its own this cable changes nothing you hear; the preamp output is not connected yet.

steps.title: Feed the saturated copy back in
steps.why:
The saturated copy goes back into the filters, so the riff is heard through two stages of distortion: one inside the filter and one in the loop.
- Cable ESP OUT (before the filter) → EXT SIGNAL IN: the processor’s first output is the preamp output. EXT SIGNAL IN joins the oscillators at the filter input, so each note is filtered, saturated and filtered again.
- Listen for: the held part of each note gains a torn, buzzing edge the filter settings alone did not give. Pull the cable to compare, or turn SIGNAL LEVEL up for more tear.

context.mix.vco1: In this sound: level and drive at once. Backing both mixer levels off cleans the riff up.
context.mix.vco2: In this sound: the octave-down saw that gives the riff its weight.
context.hpf.cutoff: In this sound: clears the rumble. Raise it towards 5 and the riff gets thin and nasal; at 0 it is heavier and muddier.
context.hpf.peak: In this sound: the nasal honk just above the high-pass cutoff.
context.lpf.cutoff: In this sound: the resting brightness between flicks.
context.lpf.peak: In this sound: the scream on each flick. Above about 8.5 it whistles over the notes.
context.lpf.type: In this sound: FILTER 2, the harder circuit. FILTER 1 gives the same shape with less bite.
context.lpmod.eg2: In this sound: the size of the "yow" at the start of each note.
context.eg2.decay: In this sound: how long the "yow" lasts.
context.esp.level: In this sound: how hard the preamp in the loop is driven, and so how torn the held tone gets.

tweaks.try: Move between 2 and 8 while the riff plays
tweaks.hear: From a riff with a little extra grit to one that buzzes and tears on every note.
The riff opens from a muffled growl to a full, bright snarl.
The weight goes and the riff turns into a thin, nasal lead.

sounds.name: Clipped Machine Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of Kraftwerk — "Numbers"
sounds.blurb: Short, identical bass notes that tick along like a machine, whatever the player does.
sounds.how: A sawtooth and a square in the same octave go through the low-pass with a little resonance. Envelope 2 has no sustain and a decay of about 70 ms, and it drives both the loudness and the low-pass cutoff. Every note is therefore the same short "dup" with the same brightness, however long the key is held. A little HOLD gives each note a flat, hard front before it drops, which keeps the line insistent rather than plucky.

steps.title: Saw and square in the same low octave
steps.why:
A sawtooth and a square make the bass: the saw for the edge, the square for weight.
- WAVE FORM (osc 1) Reverse saw, SCALE 16′: bright and buzzy, pitched low. SCALE is Korg’s octave switch, in organ-pipe feet; 16′ is the octave below normal.
- WAVE FORM (osc 2) Square, SCALE 16′, PITCH 0: a hollow square carrying the weight.
- VCO1 LEVEL 8, VCO2 LEVEL 7: both VCOs (voltage-controlled oscillators) well up. Pull VCO2 down to hear how much body the square adds.
- TIME 0: no portamento, so every note lands on its pitch.
- Listen for: a full, buzzy low tone.

steps.title: A dark, slightly resonant low-pass
steps.why:
The low-pass filter (LPF: it removes everything above its cutoff) darkens the bass, with a little resonance.
- CUTOFF (LPF) 4 · 304 Hz: how dark the note sits. Raise it and the bass turns buzzy.
- PEAK (LPF) 4.5: PEAK is Korg’s word for resonance. A slight ring on each click; above about 7 the notes start to squelch.
- FILTER 1: the rounder of the two circuits.
- CUTOFF (HPF) 0 · 12 Hz, PEAK 0: the high-pass filter (HPF) stays fully open, so the bass keeps all its weight.
- Listen for: a round, dark bass with a faint edge.

steps.title: The same short note every time
steps.why:
Envelope 2 (EG2, the main envelope) drives both loudness and the low-pass. With no sustain, every note is the same short “dup” with the same brightness, however long the key is held.
- ATTACK (EG2) 0 · 5 ms: instant.
- HOLD 1 · 21 ms: stays at full for about 20 ms first, which gives a flat, hard front. That keeps the line insistent rather than plucky.
- DECAY 3.3 · 76 ms, SUSTAIN 0: about 70 ms and gone. DECAY is the knob that makes the line clipped.
- RELEASE (EG2) 1.5 · 100 ms.
- EG2/EXT (LPF mod) 4.5: the filter follows the same shape, so each note is a bright click that closes at once.
- VOLUME 9: short notes measure quieter than held ones.
- Listen for: hold one key, then tap it. Both sound the same.

context.mix.vco2: In this sound: the square in the same octave that carries the weight.
context.lpf.cutoff: In this sound: how dark the note sits. Raise it and the bass turns buzzy.
context.lpf.peak: In this sound: a slight ring on each click. Above about 7 the notes start to squelch.
context.eg2.decay: In this sound: the length of every note. This is the knob that makes the line clipped.
context.eg2.sustain: In this sound: at 0, so held keys still give a short note.
context.eg2.hold: In this sound: the flat, hard front of each note before it drops.
context.lpmod.eg2: In this sound: how bright the click at the start of each note is.
context.out.volume: In this sound: raised because short notes measure quieter than held ones.

tweaks.hear: From a dry tick to a rounder "doom" that just touches the next note.
Every note stays full for longer before it drops, so the line pumps instead of ticking.
The clicks harden and pick up grit.

sounds.name: Gliding Lead with Late Vibrato
sounds.ref: In the style of Bernie Worrell — "Dr. Funkenstein" (The Clones of Dr. Funkenstein, 1976)
sounds.blurb: A rubbery, squelchy lead that slides between notes and only starts to wobble once a note has been held.
sounds.how: A sawtooth and a square at the same pitch go through the low-pass with plenty of PEAK, and envelope 2 flicks the cutoff open on every note for the squelch. Portamento makes every note slide up or down from the last one. The vibrato is the patch-panel part: the modulation generator goes through the spare VCA, and envelope 1, with its DELAY TIME, opens that VCA a moment after each key goes down. The delayed vibrato reaches the pitch through TOTAL, so quick notes stay straight and long ones start to wobble, the way a player brings vibrato in by hand.

steps.title: Saw and square at the same pitch
steps.why:
A sawtooth and a square at the same pitch: the saw gives the bite and the square fills out the middle.
- WAVE FORM (osc 1) Reverse saw, SCALE 8′: SCALE is Korg’s octave switch, in organ-pipe feet.
- WAVE FORM (osc 2) Square, SCALE 8′: the same octave on this oscillator.
- PITCH 0.1 · +0.2 st: a hair sharp, so the two beat slowly.
- VCO1 LEVEL 7.5, VCO2 LEVEL 6: both VCOs (voltage-controlled oscillators) well up. Pull VCO2 down for a thinner, buzzier lead.
- Listen for: a full, buzzy tone with slight movement.

steps.title: A resonant low-pass for the squelch
steps.why:
A resonant low-pass filter (LPF: it removes everything above its cutoff) sets up the squelch.
- CUTOFF (LPF) 4.8 · 524 Hz: where the tone rests between flicks. Lower is darker and more rubbery; higher is buzzier.
- PEAK (LPF) 6.5: PEAK is Korg’s word for resonance. This is the squelch; past about 8 it whistles over the notes.
- FILTER 1: the rounder circuit.
- CUTOFF (HPF) 0 · 12 Hz, PEAK 0: the high-pass filter (HPF) is fully open, so the lead keeps its body.
- Listen for: a dark tone with a resonant, rubbery ring.

steps.title: Flick the filter on every note
steps.why:
Envelope 2 (EG2, the main envelope) opens the low-pass at the start of each note and lets it fall back. That rise and fall is the squelch.
- EG2/EXT (LPF mod) 5.5: how far each flick opens the filter.
- ATTACK (EG2) 0 · 5 ms: instant.
- HOLD 0, DECAY 5 · 300 ms, SUSTAIN 5: falls back over about a third of a second to a middling level. DECAY is how long the “wow” takes.
- RELEASE (EG2) 3 · 250 ms.
- VOLUME 8.5.
- Listen for: a “wow” on the front of each note.

steps.title: Slide between notes
steps.why:
Portamento makes every note slide from the last.
- TIME 2.2: a slide of about a quarter of a second. At 0 the lead steps; above 4 it lags badly behind the riff.
- Listen for: play the riff and hear the rubbery swoops up and down between notes.

steps.title: Vibrato on the pitch
steps.why:
The modulation generator (MG, Korg’s name for the LFO, a low-frequency oscillator) is put on the pitch as a wide vibrato.
- WAVE FORM (MG) 5 · triangle, FREQUENCY 7.4 · 5.41 Hz: a smooth wobble at about 5.5 Hz.
- MG/T.EXT (pitch) 2.2: a wide vibrato.
- MG/T.EXT (HPF mod) 0, (LPF mod) 0: kept at 0. In the next step a cable in TOTAL will feed all three of these knobs, and only the pitch should move. Turning the low-pass one up would add a wah.
- Listen for: for now it wobbles all the time, including on the short notes.

steps.title: Bring the vibrato in late
steps.why:
Three cables make the vibrato arrive late, the way a player brings it in by hand.
- Cable MG OUT (triangle) → VCA IN: the wobble goes into the spare VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) on the patch panel.
- Cable EG 1 OUT → CONTROL INPUT: envelope 1 (EG1) decides how much gets through.
- Cable VCA OUT → TOTAL: replaces the modulation generator at every MG/T.EXT knob.
- DELAY TIME 5.5 · 320 ms: how long a note stays straight first.
- ATTACK (EG1) 5 · 220 ms, RELEASE 2 · 110 ms: how quickly the vibrato grows, and goes.
- EG1/EXT 0: envelope 1 stays off the pitch directly.
- Listen for: short notes are now straight; long ones wobble once settled.

context.lpf.peak: In this sound: the squelch. Past about 8 it whistles over the notes.

context.eg2.decay: In this sound: how long the flick takes to fall back.
context.porta.time: In this sound: the slide between notes. At 0 the lead steps; above 4 it lags badly behind the riff.

Slower, lazier slides that swoop into each note.
The late vibrato also opens and closes the filter, so long notes start to wah.

sounds.name: Sawing Ring Line
sounds.ref: In the style of Brian Eno — "Sky Saw" (Another Green World, 1975)
sounds.blurb: A harsh, buzzing line that saws back and forth on every held note, with a clanging edge from ring modulation.
sounds.how: Oscillator 2 is switched to RING, so it adds the two oscillators multiplied together, tuned a tritone apart for a clanging, out-of-key edge under the sawtooth. FILTER 2 roughens it further. The sawing is the modulation generator on its sawtooth shape at about 7 Hz, sweeping the low-pass cutoff: each cycle opens the filter and snaps it shut, so the note sounds as though something is being dragged back and forth across it. This describes the rough texture of the track, not its instruments.

steps.title: A sawtooth plus ring modulation
steps.why:
A sawtooth plus ring modulation, tuned a tritone apart, gives a clanging, out-of-key edge under the note.
- WAVE FORM (osc 1) Reverse saw, SCALE 8′, VCO1 LEVEL 7: the note itself, bright and buzzy. SCALE is Korg’s octave switch, in organ-pipe feet; VCO means voltage-controlled oscillator.
- WAVE FORM (osc 2) RING: replaces Oscillator 2 with the two oscillators multiplied together, which adds tones that are not in the key.
- SCALE (osc 2) 8′, PITCH 2.5 · +6 st: a tritone. 2.92 is a fifth, which is smoother; odd settings clang more.
- VCO2 LEVEL 5.5: now the amount of ring modulation. Above about 7 the clang drowns the note.
- TIME 0.8: a short portamento slide.
- Listen for: a harsh, metallic buzz.

steps.title: Thin it and rough it up
steps.why:
The filters thin the line out and rough it up.
- CUTOFF (HPF) 3.5 · 135 Hz, PEAK 3: the high-pass filter (HPF) removes everything below its cutoff, so the line sits in the middle like a treated guitar. PEAK is Korg’s word for resonance; here it adds a nasal honk.
- CUTOFF (LPF) 5.5 · 843 Hz: the low-pass filter (LPF) removes everything above.
- PEAK (LPF) 5.5: how much each saw stroke rings as it passes, once the sawing is added.
- FILTER 2: the rougher circuit, which distorts sooner than FILTER 1.
- Listen for: a thinner, grittier, more nasal tone.

steps.title: Held notes, quick start
steps.why:
Envelope 2 (EG2, the main envelope that opens the amplifier) holds notes so the sawing has time to be heard.
- ATTACK (EG2) 3 · 50 ms: takes the click off.
- HOLD 0, DECAY 6 · 690 ms, SUSTAIN 8: a high held level.
- RELEASE (EG2) 4.5 · 630 ms: a short tail.
- EG2/EXT (LPF mod) 2: a slight brightening on each note.
- VOLUME 8.
- Listen for: steady held notes, still static in tone.

steps.title: Saw at the filter
steps.why:
The modulation generator (MG, Korg’s name for the LFO, a low-frequency oscillator) sweeps the low-pass on its sawtooth shape. Each cycle opens the filter and snaps it shut, like something dragged back and forth across the note.
- WAVE FORM (MG) 10 · saw: fully clockwise. Each stroke rises and snaps back; triangle gives a smoother wobble.
- FREQUENCY 7.9 · 7.09 Hz: about seven strokes a second. Below 6 it becomes a slow pulsing; above 9 a buzz.
- MG/T.EXT (LPF mod) 5: how deep each stroke is.
- MG/T.EXT (HPF mod) 0, (pitch) 0: only the low-pass moves.
- Listen for: held notes now saw back and forth. Sweep FREQUENCY to hear it go from pulse to buzz.

tweaks.try: Move between 6 and 9.5 while a note holds
tweaks.hear: From a slow stuttering pulse to a fast, angry rasp.
The ring tones line up as a fifth, so the clang turns into a hard, organ-like buzz.
Reverse sawtooth: each stroke snaps open and falls away, so the sawing runs the other way.

sounds.name: Sliding Steel Swell
sounds.ref: In the style of Daniel Lanois — "Transmitter" (Shine, 2003)
sounds.blurb: A warm, slow-swelling note that slides into each new pitch and fades out over several seconds, like a pedal steel played with a volume pedal.
sounds.how: Two sawtooths at the same octave, a few cents apart, beat slowly for warmth, and the low-pass takes off the top so nothing is sharp. Envelope 2 has an attack of about a second, so each note swells in rather than being plucked, and a long release lets it fade. PORTAMENTO makes the pitch slide from note to note like a steel bar moving along the strings, and a slight vibrato keeps held notes alive. This describes the style of playing, not the exact sound on the record.

steps.title: Two sawtooths, slightly apart
steps.why:
Two sawtooths at the same octave, a few cents apart, beat slowly for warmth.
- WAVE FORM Reverse saw on both, SCALE 8′ on both: SCALE is Korg’s octave switch, in organ-pipe feet.
- PITCH 0.1 · +0.2 st: Oscillator 2 a hair sharp. Larger offsets sound like a chorus, then out of tune.
- VCO1 LEVEL 6.5, VCO2 LEVEL 5.5: both VCOs (voltage-controlled oscillators) in, the second a little lower.
- Listen for: a bright tone with a slow, warm swirl.

steps.title: Round off the top
steps.why:
The filters round off the top so nothing is sharp.
- CUTOFF (LPF) 5.6 · 902 Hz: the low-pass filter (LPF) removes everything above its cutoff. This is how warm the tone is; raise it for a brighter, more metallic steel.
- PEAK (LPF) 1.5, FILTER 1: PEAK is Korg’s word for resonance; only a little.
- EG2/EXT (LPF mod) 2.5: envelope 2 (EG2) brightens the tone slightly as each note swells.
- CUTOFF (HPF) 2 · 48 Hz, PEAK 0: the high-pass filter (HPF) trims only the lowest rumble.
- Listen for: a warmer, softer tone.

steps.title: Swell in, fade out slowly
steps.why:
Envelope 2 (EG2, the main envelope that opens the amplifier) swells each note in like a volume pedal and lets it fade slowly.
- ATTACK (EG2) 7 · 970 ms: about a second to reach full, the way a player eases a volume pedal down. Lower it and notes start with a plucked edge.
- HOLD 0, DECAY 7.5 · 2.3 s, SUSTAIN 8: a gentle ease-off to a high held level.
- RELEASE (EG2) 7.5 · 3.9 s: each note fades over a few seconds after you let go.
- VOLUME 9.
- Listen for: notes swelling in with no attack and overlapping as they fade.

steps.title: Slide like a steel bar
steps.why:
Portamento makes each note slide from the last, like a steel bar moving along the strings.
- TIME 3.5: a slide of about half a second. At 0 the notes step; above 5 the slide is slower than the melody.
- Listen for: because the swell is slow too, you hear the slide as the new note fades up.

steps.title: A slight vibrato
steps.why:
A slight vibrato from the modulation generator (MG, Korg’s name for the LFO, a low-frequency oscillator) keeps held notes alive.
- WAVE FORM (MG) 5 · triangle, FREQUENCY 7 · 4.36 Hz: a smooth waver at about 4.5 Hz.
- MG/T.EXT (pitch) 1.2: just enough to shimmer without sounding out of tune. Keep it below 2.
- MG/T.EXT (HPF mod) 0, (LPF mod) 0: the filters stay still.
- Listen for: long notes shimmer gently once they have swelled in.

context.eg2.release: In this sound: the long fade after each note.

context.lpf.cutoff: In this sound: how warm the tone is. Raise it for a brighter, more metallic steel.
context.lpmod.eg2: In this sound: a small brightening as each note swells.
context.fmod.mg: In this sound: vibrato depth. Keep it below 2.

tweaks.hear: From a quick swell to a note that takes two seconds to arrive.
A short slide into each note, more like a small bar movement.
A brighter, more metallic tone, closer to a steel guitar through a clean amp.
